summary: 2 ideas judged, none passed (1 reached confirmation). Closest: Daily-EMA recovery swing, only when SPY is up on the day (failed confirmation). The ledger holds 21 ideas; 12 have reached confirmation, so the next one there needs t >= 2.67.

ideas.title: Daily-EMA recovery swing, only when SPY is up on the day
ideas.hypothesis: The daily-EMA reclaim is a long-only dip-buy, and it needs the market behind it: on discovery the worst fifth of recovery-swing trades by SPY's intraday move (SPY well below its open) averages about -0.26R while every other fifth is positive, and the one candidate that reached confirmation was strong in the first half and flat in the second, the signature of a strategy that depends on the market's direction. Refusing the setup whenever SPY is below its own session open should drop roughly the worst 40% of trades and lift the per-trade margin over random entries enough to carry the whole period rather than one regime.
ideas.builds_on: re-a9765cdc93 (daily-EMA recovery swing, no trigger on the session's first bar; failed screen at t=1.97 with avg +0.18R)
ideas.change: One filter added: take the signal only when spy_day is at or above 0, i.e. SPY is trading above its own session open at the signal bar's close. Trigger level (daily EMA), the 10:00 start of the window, arming, breakout confirmation, stop, 2R target and two-session hold are all unchanged.

ideas.title: Daily-EMA recovery swing held a third session
ideas.hypothesis: The forward evidence for this entry says its edge accrues slowly and keeps growing: against random entries the move after the fill is +0.03R at 30 minutes, +0.05R at an hour, +0.11R at the session close and +0.21R at the next session's close, with no sign of fading. That is a multi-day recovery, not an intraday pop, and the matching failure is the stall exit, which cut trades at one hour and died in confirmation. Exiting at the second session's close therefore closes trades that are still working; giving the same trades a third session should let more of them reach the 2R target and widen the gap over random entries, which are held exactly as long.

answer.lessons: Nothing has passed yet, and the forward evidence now tells us which patterns are worth any more work. The two one-minute patterns, the VWAP reclaim and the failed breakout, move barely at all in our favour after the fill at any horizon, so no target, hold or timeframe change can rescue them; they are finished. The opening range breakout has a real but tiny edge that lives only in the first fifteen minutes after the break and is gone by thirty, and that edge is smaller than the round-trip cost, so it cannot pay for itself either. The recovery swing triggered on the prior day's daily EMA is the only idea that makes money before costs, about +0.15 to +0.18R a trade, and its edge grows the longer the trade is held, right out to the next session's close, which is why the one-hour stall exit that passed the screen then collapsed in the second half of confirmation. That collapse was a regime split, so this week's main test is the obvious market rule, taking the long only when SPY itself is up on the day, with a companion test that holds the same trades a third session instead of two. The confirmation bar is t >= 2.64 and rises with each arrival, so with roughly 400 trades a candidate now needs about a quarter of an R per trade over random entries, which only a real improvement in trade quality can deliver.
wanted: A way to take the opposite side of a family's signal (a fade or invert switch): the VWAP reclaim's entries move against their own direction by -0.87R into the next session's close with t = -2.7, which is the strongest single number in the discovery evidence and we cannot trade it.
Swing-scale exits for multi-session holds: a stop or target measured in daily ATR, a trailing stop on the daily EMA being lost, and max_sessions beyond 3.

A partial exit (take half at 1R, let the rest run): the recovery swing's median best price before the close is only about 0.5R while its edge keeps growing for days, so the all-or-nothing 2R target is probably the wrong shape.
An earnings or scheduled-event flag, so multi-session holds can avoid carrying a position through a report.
A slower market-regime feature, such as SPY's return over the prior five or twenty sessions, to separate trend from chop at a scale above spy_day and spy_trend.
